question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound recipient allowlist for Slack message sends now, and should that policy live in Slack config or in a shared human-chat outbound target policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding this guardrail changes public config and outbound authorization semantics under a security-sensitive trusted-operator model, so automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Add explicit outbound target policy
options.body: Add a documented allowTo-style outbound recipient policy with schema, docs, tests, and enforcement at the shared outbound/channel send boundary.

options.title: Fold into broader outbound guardrails
options.body: Track Slack recipient allowlisting as an acceptance case under #87870 so sanitizer, verified delivery, and target authorization are designed together.

options.title: Decline core allowTo for now
options.body: Keep the current trusted-operator model and document that `dmPolicy` and `allowFrom` do not constrain explicit operator sends.

recommendation.title: Add explicit outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented allowTo-style outbound recipient policy with schema, docs, tests, and enforcement at the shared outbound/channel send boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The outbound policy, message delivery, and Slack DM access history make this the best available owner for the config/security boundary decision.
